key_facts: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
generated_text: Introduction to Structured Query Language (SQL) Structured Query Language, or SQL, is the standard computer language for managing relational databases and manipulating the data they contain. It allows you to define the structure of your data, modify the data itself, and control who has access to it. SQL is fundamentally divided into three basic sub-languages: Data Definition Language (DDL) Data Manipulation Language (DML) Data Control Language (DCL) Data Definition Language (DDL) DDL commands are used to define and manage the structure of your database and its objects. These commands allow you to specify data types, create relationships between tables, and enforce constraints on the data. All these specifications are stored directly within the database. The core DDL commands are: CREATE: Used to build a new database object, such as a table, schema, index, or user. ALTER: Used to modify the structure of an existing database object, for example, by adding a new column to a table. DROP: Used to permanently delete an existing database object from the database. Data Manipulation Language (DML) DML commands are used to manage the data stored within the database objects. These are the commands you will use most frequently for day-to-day operations like querying and modifying data. The core DML commands are: SELECT: Retrieves information from a database. This is the most commonly used SQL command. INSERT: Adds new rows of data into a table. UPDATE: Modifies existing data within a table. DELETE: Removes rows of data from a table. Data Control Language (DCL) DCL commands are used to manage database security and transaction integrity. They control which users have access to which data and how changes to the data are managed. The core DCL commands include: GRANT: Gives specific permissions (e.g., SELECT, INSERT) on a database object to a user. REVOKE: Removes permissions from a user. COMMIT: Saves all the changes made during the current transaction, making them permanent. ROLLBACK: Undoes all the changes made during the current transaction, reverting the database to its previous state. Summary Understanding the three main components of SQL is essential for working with relational databases. DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) is used to build and define the database structure. DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) is used to query and manipulate the data within that structure. Finally, DCL (GRANT, REVOKE, COMMIT, ROLLBACK) is used to manage access rights and control transactions. Mastering these commands provides a complete foundation for database management.
